author: NorthEast News Desk
body: The National Institutes of Health has awarded $26 million to renew Rhode Island's statewide clinical and translational research hub for another five years. Brown University hosts Advance RI-CTR, which links academic institutions, health systems and community organizations to move discoveries from laboratories toward clinical and community use.

The third phase will provide researchers with consultation in quantitative and qualitative methods, implementation science, artificial intelligence and digital health. It will also broaden regional and national partnerships, offer multiple funding mechanisms for emerging research leaders and expand access to data and other research resources. Participating institutions include Brown, the University of Rhode Island, Brown University Health, Care New England and the Providence VA system.

Since 2016, the program says $11.2 million awarded to Rhode Island investigators has helped them secure another $132.4 million in public and private funding. It has supported 141 investigators, contributed to six commercial patents and trained more than 340 research mentors. The renewal is intended to deepen that infrastructure while giving community priorities a larger role in deciding which health questions move from research into practice.
dek: The five-year NIH award will fund a third phase of Advance RI-CTR, expanding research support, partnerships and community engagement.
headline: $26 million grant renews statewide Rhode Island clinical-research network
